actions.action: Reserve non-evictable capacity for critical history.
actions.mechanism: Separate allocation prevents ordinary-event volume from consuming space required by critical events.
actions.implementation: Within 20 MB, reserve 2 MB plus bounded encoding overhead for critical records. Give ordinary data only the remainder; reclaim critical records only after durable acknowledgement.
actions.check: Generate maximum ordinary traffic and 2 MB of critical events during a 30-minute outage; verify every critical sequence survives.
actions.risk: Capacity accounting must include indexes, framing, and recovery metadata.

actions.action: Replace ordinary detail with explicit coverage summaries.
actions.mechanism: Bounded summaries identify intervals where ordinary records were omitted without retaining their contents.
actions.implementation: Use a rotating ordinary buffer and preallocated time-bucket summaries containing sequence ranges, retained counts, and omitted counts. Allowlist diagnostic fields; reject bodies, credentials, and user content.
actions.check: Force repeated buffer rollover; verify every omitted ordinary sequence falls within a marked reduced-detail interval and prohibited fields never persist.
actions.risk: Summary granularity limits how precisely omissions can be located.

actions.action: Make replay identity stable across upload retries.
actions.mechanism: Persistent record identities separate duplicate delivery from missing records; coverage manifests expose trailing gaps.
actions.implementation: Assign installation-epoch, stream, and sequence identities. Upload a bounded manifest of sequence high-water marks and reduction intervals; deduplicate transactionally before acknowledging durable receipt.
actions.check: Replay with duplicate batches, lost acknowledgements, and one deleted critical record. Require one logical copy per identity and detection of the deletion.
actions.risk: Reused identities or premature acknowledgements can conceal missing data.

actions.action: Test recoverability through the actual reader.
actions.mechanism: Non-destructive recovery drills verify that retained critical bytes remain decodable and replayable, not merely present.
actions.implementation: Use versioned, checksummed records and committed-length markers. Periodically read committed critical records without deleting them; exercise the production recovery and upload paths in fault-injection tests.
actions.check: Interrupt writes and acknowledgements across a 30-minute test. Verify all committed critical sequences recover and corruption is reported rather than silently skipped.
actions.risk: Checksums detect damage; they cannot guarantee survival of physical storage failure.
